title: Sell-side global markets functional architecture (layered view, pre-trade to post-trade)

bands.name: Common services

assumptions: Archetype: a global bank's markets division (sales and trading only) with UK, EU and US legal entities, dealing as principal and agent across EQ, FI, FX and DR.
Out of scope: primary issuance (ECM/DCM), research production, corporate and retail banking, treasury ALM beyond trading funding, and agentic AI.

The bank runs its own custody business (L5, owner stage S7), so custody components are internal; CSDs, ICSDs, CCPs, CLS, agent banks, trade repositories, triparty agents, data vendors and the messaging network are third-party run and appear as external parties. Four FMI touchpoints (C28, C41, C49, C50) are drawn inside their lifecycle layer (L4, L5) to show the flow; they are the same parties as X13, X04, X05 and X07.

The architecture is a functional layer view, read top to bottom from pre-trade to post-trade: three lifecycle bands (B1 to B3, five layers), one cross-lifecycle band (B4, two layers) and one common services band (B5, one layer). The owner's 10-stage Trade Flow Value Chain is kept only as a traceability tag ('stages') on every layer and group. A trade does not pass every lifecycle layer: FX skips custody, OTC uncleared skips CCP clearing, listed derivatives skip CSD settlement.
Asset-class tags: EQ equities, FI fixed income (rates and credit), FX, DR derivatives (OTC and listed); ALL when common to all four.
external=true means usually run by a third party. The bank keeps oversight through C96 Third-Party and FMI Oversight, C51 Agent Bank Management and C95 Operational Resilience.

Regulatory reporting is produced and controlled in one cross-lifecycle layer, L7: G13 holds transaction, derivative, transparency and SFTR reporting (C35, C36, C37, C66) with the reporting control hub (C91). Surveillance and the control room (P6) and conduct and client assets oversight (G27) sit in L7 as second-line functions.
Cross-reference fields are left blank where no honest match exists. BIAN names are labels from v10, not structure; several are closest fit.
FIX names are FIX Latest MsgType names; iso20022 lists business areas only, not message versions; swift_mt numbers are unverified analyst knowledge.
Links are illustrative key flows in three threads; the real integration estate is far denser and most components read from the platform.
No vendor product names and no statistics. Regimes marked not verified were not checked against the source for this draft and should be validated before external use.

Office assignment is a convention; banks differ (for example some run prime services or clearing under Middle Office). Layer office is the dominant owner; each group keeps its own office from the stage view.

Financing is not the last step of a trade. Securities lending, repo, prime margin lending and synthetic financing finance positions that already exist, from trade date to settlement and for as long as the position is held, and collateral, liquidity and cash serve margin (L4), settlement (L5) and financing alike. They form cross-lifecycle layer L6, not a stage after custody.

Market data is not a step in the trade. Prices, curves and ticks are consumed by quoting (L2), execution and algos (L3), margin (L4), valuation and risk (L7) and surveillance (L7), so market data sits in common services (L8) beside reference data and is available to every layer.

Risk, control and regulatory reporting are not a step between confirmation and clearing. Limits gate onboarding and pre-trade checks, reports are due at execution and on lifecycle events, and surveillance reads orders as well as trades, so they form cross-lifecycle layer L7.

Reconciliation is a shared service (L8, G28): C99 reconciles front to back and against CCPs, clearing brokers, triparty agents and counterparties, and C53 reconciles nostros and depots, so both read from every lifecycle layer and from L6. OTC portfolio reconciliation (C30) stays in L4 because it is a bilateral confirmation duty with counterparties.

The 'stages' tag on a group names where its content sits on the owner's current slides: S0 to S9 for the stage strip and PLATFORM for the cross-cutting platform strip. Each group also carries 'origin' (old stage or platform group).

Slide fit: seven layer rows for the lifecycle and cross-lifecycle bands (L1 to L7), with common services (L8) drawn as one foundation strip beneath them, as the platform was before. L1 and L2 are kept apart, while L3 merges execution with trading and booking, L4 merges confirmation with clearing and L5 merges settlement with custody.

Links, threads and component fields are unchanged; links gain from_layer and to_layer, externals gain layers, and standards gain the layers that use them. Verified and unverified flags are exactly as before.

families.BIAN: Strong: Customer Relationship Management, Party Lifecycle Management, Counterparty Risk, Customer Agreement, Customer Access Entitlement. No domain for KYC screening, client categorisation or SSIs.
families.CALM: Services, systems and databases; client is an actor.
families.FIX: IOI for axes; SettlementInstructions and SettlementInstructionRequest for standing instructions only; onboarding itself is not a FIX process.
families.FpML_CDM: CDM legal agreements model for CSA elections.
families.ISO20022: Not used here in this map (acmt applies to custody accounts in L5).
families.other: KYC/AML and MiFID categorisation (unverified); no data standard for KYC files.

families.BIAN: Good: Quote Management, Market Making, Suitability Checking, Product Design; Trading Models is closest fit. No domain for the single-dealer platform.
families.CALM: Engagement services and web clients; multi-dealer platforms are ecosystem externals.
families.FIX: QuoteRequest, Quote, QuoteResponse; NewOrderSingle through the client channel.
families.FpML_CDM: Product model for structured and OTC trades.
families.other: MiFID suitability, appropriateness, costs and charges (unverified).

families.BIAN: Strong: Market Order, Market Order Execution, Program Trading, eTrading Workbench, Trader Position Operations; Commissions for fees and billing. No domain for pre-trade controls, DMA, FX aggregation, venue gateways, booking or enrichment.
families.CALM: Systems, services, web clients and network gateways.
families.FIX: Core: NewOrderSingle, ExecutionReport, Quote; TradeCaptureReport at booking.
families.FpML_CDM: CDM event model at execution feeds booking and derivative reporting.
families.ISO20022: None (setr is fund and securities trade initiation, used little on sell-side execution).

families.BIAN: Good: Order Allocation, Trade Confirmation Matching, Trade Clearing, Credit and Margin Management, Collateral Allocation Management. No domain for portfolio reconciliation, lifecycle events, structured products lifecycle, client clearing or compression.
families.CALM: Services and systems; matching utility and CCP are ecosystems.
families.FIX: AllocationInstruction, AllocationReport, Confirmation, ConfirmationAck, TradeCaptureReport, PositionReport, CollateralReport, MarginRequirementReport.

stage_traceability.name: Onboarding
stage_traceability.note: Pre-trade: onboarding, KYC, credit and documentation sit in L1 with sales coverage.
stage_traceability.purpose_on_slide: Make a client legally, credit and operationally ready to trade.
stage_traceability.value_on_slide: Cost sits here: onboarding time delays first trade and revenue; credit and documentation set the capital each client consumes.

stage_traceability.name: Origination
stage_traceability.note: Pre-trade: coverage moves to L1 beside onboarding; quoting, pricing and structuring form L2.
stage_traceability.purpose_on_slide: Win secondary-market client business: coverage, quoting, structuring and suitability (primary issuance out of scope)
stage_traceability.value_on_slide: Margin sits here: bid-offer spread on flow and structuring margin on bespoke products.

stage_traceability.name: Execution
stage_traceability.note: Trade: order, execution and trading desk groups form L3; venue gateways now sit with routing.
stage_traceability.purpose_on_slide: Execute orders and quotes with control and best execution.
stage_traceability.value_on_slide: Margin sits here: internalisation, execution quality and electronic scale; cost sits in venue fees and errors.

stage_traceability.name: Confirmation
stage_traceability.note: Split across bands: booking is a trade-date function in L3; allocation, confirmation and OTC lifecycle are post-trade in L4.
stage_traceability.purpose_on_slide: Book, allocate, confirm and agree every trade with the client.
stage_traceability.value_on_slide: Cost sits here: breaks, late confirmations and manual affirmation drive operational risk and headcount.

stage_traceability.name: Risk and Reporting
stage_traceability.note: Not a sequential step: risk, P&L and regulatory reporting run across the lifecycle in L7, which also takes SFTR reporting and the reporting control hub.
stage_traceability.purpose_on_slide: Measure risk and P&L and report every trade to regulators and markets.
stage_traceability.value_on_slide: Cost sits here: reporting errors bring fines and remediation; capital follows measured risk.

stage_traceability.name: Clearing
stage_traceability.note: Post-trade: clearing and margin sit in L4 with confirmation.
stage_traceability.purpose_on_slide: Novate eligible trades to CCPs and manage margin and netting.
stage_traceability.value_on_slide: Cost sits here: margin funding, CCP fees and capital; client clearing earns fees.

stage_traceability.name: Settlement
stage_traceability.note: Post-trade: settlement sits in L5 with custody.
stage_traceability.purpose_on_slide: Exchange securities and cash with finality, on time.
stage_traceability.value_on_slide: Cost sits here: fails, CSDR penalties, buy-ins and intraday funding.

stage_traceability.name: Custody
stage_traceability.note: Post-trade: custody and asset servicing sit in L5; client money and assets oversight is a control in L7.
stage_traceability.purpose_on_slide: Safekeep and service client and firm assets held by the bank.
stage_traceability.value_on_slide: Fees sit here: safekeeping and asset servicing; cost sits in corporate action errors and missed claims.

stage_traceability.name: Financing and Prime
stage_traceability.note: Not a final step: financing and prime act on positions from trade date to settlement and beyond, so they form cross-lifecycle layer L6 with collateral, liquidity and cash; SFTR reporting moves to L7.
stage_traceability.purpose_on_slide: Finance client and firm positions through lending, repo and synthetics.
stage_traceability.value_on_slide: Margin sits here: lending fees, repo spreads and financing on balances; cost sits in balance sheet.

stage_traceability.name: Market Data
stage_traceability.note: Not a step at all: market data feeds every layer, so it sits in the common services layer L8.
stage_traceability.purpose_on_slide: Feeds every stage: acquire, distribute and license the data every price and risk number uses.
stage_traceability.value_on_slide: Cost sits here: data licences, colocation and low-latency infrastructure.

stage_traceability.name: Cross-cutting platform
stage_traceability.note: The former cross-cutting platform is split by purpose: risk and limits, surveillance, conduct and client assets join L7; collateral, liquidity and cash join L6; the rest form L8 common services.

CALM.note: Every component has a CALM 1.1 node type.

FIX.note: MsgType names checked against a FIX Latest dictionary.

FpML_CDM.note: Family level (FpML; CDM product, event, legal, collateral, repo); not message level.

ISO20022.note: Business areas only; message identifiers not checked.

regs.note: See standards list for verified flag per regime.

gaps: No open standard for KYC due-diligence data or onboarding workflow

No BIAN domain for KYC screening, trade booking/enrichment, front-to-back reconciliation, control room, structured products lifecycle, single-dealer platform, surveillance, best execution, client clearing, compression, locates, TRS, rehypothecation, client assets, data lineage or valuation adjustments
No messaging standard for pre-trade risk controls, internal P&L, product control or IPV
No open standard for market data licence and usage reporting
No common standard for tax reclaim submissions
Operational resilience, third-party oversight and conduct have regulation but no data or messaging standard
ISO 20022 for sell-side execution (setr) is little used; FIX dominates
FpML/CDM cover OTC derivatives, repo, lending and collateral, not cash equity or bond settlement
